name: Al Masraf (Arab Bank for Investment and Foreign Trade)
legal_name: Arab Bank for Investment and Foreign Trade PJSC
founded: 1976 (Union Decree No. 50 of 1976; joint venture of the UAE, Libya and Algeria)
ownership_summary: Unlisted PJSC with three shareholders. The Emirates Investment Authority (EIA), the UAE federal government's sovereign wealth fund, holds 60.00%, Libyan Foreign Bank 29.30% and Banque Extérieure d'Algérie 10.70% (30 Jun 2026). EIA became majority owner on 6 Nov 2025 by buying 12.98% from Libyan Foreign Bank and 4.74% from Banque Extérieure d'Algérie (CBUAE-approved). Before that the split was 42.28% / 42.28% / 15.44% (31 Dec 2024).

shareholders.holder: Emirates Investment Authority (UAE federal sovereign wealth fund)

government_link: Yes: majority-owned (60%) by the Emirates Investment Authority, the only sovereign wealth fund of the UAE Federal Government (since 6 Nov 2025). The other 40% is held by Libyan and Algerian state banks. The bank calls itself 'the UAE's Federal Commercial Bank' (S4, S1, S9).
group_structure: Single bank, no subsidiaries reported. Islamic banking runs through a window launched in 2015 under a CBUAE licence for Shari'ah-compliant activities (S1, S3). Five UAE branches and two representative offices.
footprint: UAE: 5 branches and 2 representative offices (30 Jun 2026), 50+ ATMs. Trade links with Libya and Algeria. Gross loans are 70% UAE, 16% GCC and 14% other (Jun 2026) (S1, S2, S3).
customer_segments: Corporate and institutional (about 90% focus; trade finance, government-linked entities), SME/business banking, retail (salaried and self-employed), and an affluent 'Elite Banking' tier.
business_lines: Corporate/wholesale banking and trade finance (AED 23bn of export LCs processed in 2025); Treasury & Investments (FX, rate hedging, bonds/sukuk trading and fixed-income custody); Retail & Business Banking (accounts, fixed deposits, personal, auto and home loans, cards, salary transfer); Elite Banking; Islamic window. Consumer gross loans were only AED 558m of AED 18.99bn at 30 Jun 2026 (S1). Consumer deposits exceeded AED 2bn and business banking deposits AED 1.4bn in 2025 (S3).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Al Masraf is a corporate and trade-finance bank (about 90% corporate focus; consumer loans 3% of gross loans) that became majority-owned by the UAE federal sovereign wealth fund EIA in Nov 2025. Its affluent tier, Elite Banking, needs AED 1m in combined deposits and investments (self-employed) or AED 80,000 monthly salary. It offers a dedicated RM and a 'diverse investment product suite' and 'wealth management services', but no specific products are named. Treasury & Investments offers bonds and sukuk, secondary trading, fixed-income custody and FX; FX spot is open to all segments, forwards and swaps are not for individuals. No funds platform, brokerage, digital investing or discretionary service was found. The 2025 report mentions a 'multi-product investment platform' only as a treasury execution tool.

segments.name: Elite Banking
segments.eligibility: Self-employed: combined deposits and investments of 1 million or more (currency not stated); salaried: monthly salary of at least AED 80,000

segments.name: Personal Banking
segments.eligibility: Salary-transfer and self-employed customers (accounts, loans, cards)

private_banking.detail: No private banking unit; Elite Banking is the top tier.

asset_management.detail: No asset management entity or own funds. 'Funds management' in the treasury segment refers to managing the bank's own portfolio.

brokerage.detail: Treasury makes markets in regional bonds and sukuk, executes secondary trades and offers fixed-income custody; no equity brokerage found. Target client segments for fixed income are not stated.

digital_investing.detail: Mobile/online banking supports accounts, payments, cards and digital account opening; no investing features found. Enhanced mobile banking is a 2026 programme.

advisory.detail: Elite page promises 'Wealth Management Services' and an investment product suite through a dedicated RM, with no detail; the 2025 report mentions training to build 'frontline advisory capabilities'.

structured_products.detail: Only FX and interest-rate hedging (forwards and swaps not for individuals).

private_markets.detail: None found. A Mastercard x Stake card offer (credit toward a first real-estate investment on Stake) is a card promotion, not a bank product.

islamic_wealth.detail: Islamic window since 2015 with personal accounts, cards and finance; sukuk are offered by Treasury, but no Islamic wealth product for individuals was found.

partners.what: Supply chain financing platform for corporate clients, signed at GTR MENA 2025

initiatives.what: Emirates Investment Authority raised its stake to 60% (buying 12.98% from Libyan Foreign Bank and 4.74% from Banque Extérieure d'Algérie), CBUAE-approved

Delivered UAE PASS authentication, AANI payments, digitised AML risk scoring; launched a 'Future Makers' digital programme; Treasury roadmap includes a modern treasury management system and a multi-product investment platform

Programmes running into 2026: enhanced mobile banking, digital trade journeys, open finance, core banking modernisation and end-to-end corporate lending transformation; strategy statement: 'UAE's Federal Commercial Bank', corporate-led, backed by retail and SME growth plans
Board and management reshuffle after the ownership change: Mohamed Saif Al Suwaidi became Chairman; two new directors; Ahmad Yousuf moved to Chief Retail Banking Officer

opportunities: Elite Banking (AED 1m balances or AED 80k monthly salary) advertises a 'diverse investment product suite' and wealth services but names no products, platform or partners (S6).

New federal majority owner (EIA, Nov 2025) and a reshuffled board and management, with a new Chief Retail Banking Officer, point to a strategy reset where retail and SME growth plans 'back' the corporate agenda (S4, S5).
Open finance, enhanced mobile banking and core banking modernisation are 2026 programmes, so new integrations are being planned (S3).
barriers: Retail is tiny: consumer gross loans AED 558m of AED 19bn (Jun 2026); consumer deposits about AED 2bn (2025) (S1, S3).
Strategy is explicitly corporate and trade-finance led (S3, S4).
Only five branches; no digital investing features in the app (S1, S8).
